sentences.text: (3) As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of grievous injury of respondent/claimant Arun Rathore, the amount of compensation has been allowed by the Tribunal in favour of claimant/respondent of Rs.1,01,800/- at the rate of interest 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.

(4) Counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal on the ground that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not considering that in pertinent matter Insurance Policy produced by the owner of offending vehicle is not authentic and it is a fictitious document produced by owner of offending vehicle.

(5) It is also averred that learned Tribunal has awarded the compensation in favour of respondents without giving adequate opportunity to appellant for proper verification and scrutinization of Insurance Policy and hence the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation because the insurance policy was fake and the Insurance Company has not issued the policy and hence prays for setting aside the impugned award against the Insurance Company.
(6) Per contra, counsel for the respondents/claimants has supported the impugned award and prays for rejection of the appeal.
(7) After hearing counsel for both the parties, it was found that the Insurance Company has filed this appeal on the ground that the policy produced by the owner of offending vehicle was fake and authentic and it was also found that the Insurance Company is unable to produce any evidence in this regard.
The Insurance Company has unable to produce any document before the Court that policy was obtained by fraud or the same is not authentic.
(8) So in view of lack of evidence by Insurance Company regarding the fact that the Company was unable to prove that the policy was not authentic.
So in the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has rightly awarded the award and hence no interference is called for by this Court.
Accordingly, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company stands dismissed.
